q: What does the scheduler use to decide whether a pod fits on a node?
options: The node's current actual CPU and memory usage from metrics-server
The pod's requests compared with the node's allocatable capacity minus requests of pods already there
The pod's limits compared with the node's capacity
The number of pods on the node only
explain: Scheduling is purely request-based. A node with idle CPU can still be "full" if its requests add up to allocatable. Limits are enforced at runtime, not used for fitting.

q: Your NestJS API has a CPU limit of `500m`. Average CPU is 30%, but p99 latency is high during bursts. What is the most likely explanation?
options: The pod is being OOMKilled
The readiness probe is failing
CFS throttling: bursts exhaust the 50 ms per 100 ms quota and the process is paused
The node is out of memory
explain: CPU limits throttle within each 100 ms period. Averages hide this. Check `nr_throttled` in `cpu.stat` or `container_cpu_cfs_throttled_periods_total`, and consider raising or removing the CPU limit.

q: A container's last state shows `exitCode: 137, reason: OOMKilled`. What happened?
options: The kernel killed the process because the container exceeded its memory limit
The V8 heap limit was reached
The kubelet evicted the pod due to disk pressure
The liveness probe failed
explain: 137 = 128 + SIGKILL(9), and `OOMKilled` means the cgroup memory limit was hit. A V8 heap OOM aborts with exit 134 and a `JavaScript heap out of memory` message instead.

q: A pod has two containers. Container A has CPU and memory requests equal to limits. Container B has no resources set. What is the pod's QoS class?
options: Guaranteed
It depends on the node
BestEffort
Burstable
explain: Guaranteed requires every container to have CPU and memory requests equal to limits. BestEffort requires no container to have any. Anything in between is Burstable.

q: A Deployment shows `READY 3/5`. There are no Pending pods and no warning events on the Deployment. Where do you look next?
options: The scheduler logs
The ReplicaSet's events, for example `exceeded quota` from a ResourceQuota
The kubelet logs on each node
The Service's endpoints
explain: When admission (such as a ResourceQuota or LimitRange) rejects pod creation, no pod object exists. The ReplicaSet records `FailedCreate` events with the reason.

q: A pod is Pending with: `0/4 nodes are available: 1 node(s) had untolerated taint {node-role.kubernetes.io/control-plane: }, 3 Insufficient memory.` Which actions could make it schedulable? (select all)
options: Lower the pod's memory request
Add nodes or free memory requests on existing nodes
Lower the pod's memory limit while keeping the request
Remove other pods' requests or scale down other workloads
explain: Insufficient memory refers to requests vs allocatable. Changing only the limit does not affect scheduling. Smaller requests, more capacity, or freeing requested capacity all help.

q: You taint a node `dedicated=batch:NoSchedule` and add a matching toleration to your batch Job. The Job's pods still land on other nodes. Why?
options: A toleration only allows scheduling onto the tainted node; you also need a nodeSelector or node affinity to attract the pods there
Tolerations only work with `NoExecute`
The taint must be applied before the node joins the cluster
Jobs ignore tolerations
explain: Taints repel, tolerations permit, affinity/nodeSelector attract. Dedicated nodes use a taint plus a label selected by the workload.

q: Six replicas use `topologySpreadConstraints` with `maxSkew: 1` across zones `a`, `b`, `c` and `DoNotSchedule`. Zone `c` only has nodes with a taint the pods do not tolerate, and no `nodeTaintsPolicy` is set. What happens?
options: 3 pods in `a` and 3 in `b`
All pods go to zone `c`
Only 2 pods run (one in `a`, one in `b`); the rest stay Pending because zone `c` counts as an empty domain
The constraint is ignored when a zone is tainted
explain: The default `nodeTaintsPolicy: Ignore` includes tainted nodes in skew calculations. Zone `c` has 0 pods, so `a` and `b` are capped at 1. Set `nodeTaintsPolicy: Honor` to exclude untolerated nodes.

q: Why does a pod running on a node that suddenly dies typically get replaced only after about five minutes?
options: The scheduler runs every five minutes
The kubelet must confirm the deletion first
The ReplicaSet controller waits for the pod's terminationGracePeriodSeconds
Pods get default tolerations for `node.kubernetes.io/not-ready` and `unreachable` with `tolerationSeconds: 300`
explain: When a node becomes NotReady/unreachable it gets `NoExecute` taints. Pods tolerate them for 300 s by default, then they are evicted and replaced. You can lower `tolerationSeconds` for faster failover.

q: A team set a PDB with `minAvailable: 3` on a 3-replica Deployment. What is the consequence?
options: Drains evict pods one at a time
No pod can ever be voluntarily evicted, so node drains, upgrades and consolidation hang
The Deployment cannot scale
The PDB is ignored by `kubectl drain`
explain: With 3 replicas and `minAvailable: 3`, zero disruptions are allowed. Use `maxUnavailable: 1` with at least 2 replicas.

q: Which statements about PriorityClasses and preemption are true? (select all)
options: A pending higher-priority pod may cause lower-priority pods to be evicted to make room
`preemptionPolicy: Never` gives a pod queue priority without evicting others
Preemption strictly guarantees PodDisruptionBudgets are never violated
Victims receive their graceful termination period
explain: Preemption tries to respect PDBs but does not guarantee it. Victims are deleted gracefully. `Never` keeps scheduling-queue priority without preempting.

q: A Node.js service runs with a 512Mi memory limit. What is a sensible heap setting?
options: `--max-old-space-size=512` so the heap can use the full limit
`--max-old-space-size=4096` to avoid heap errors
`--max-old-space-size=384`, leaving room for Buffers, native memory and stacks
No setting; the heap is unrelated to container memory
explain: Keep the heap around 70 to 80 percent of the limit. A heap as big as the limit lets total RSS exceed it, turning a clear heap error into a kernel OOMKill.

q: `kubectl top pods` returns `error: Metrics API not available`. What is missing?
options: metrics-server (serving the `metrics.k8s.io` API)
Prometheus
The Vertical Pod Autoscaler
cAdvisor must be enabled on each pod
explain: `kubectl top` and the HPA read the resource metrics API served by metrics-server. On kind it needs `--kubelet-insecure-tls` because kubelet serving certs are self-signed.

q: You add a new node to a busy cluster. What happens to existing pods?
options: The scheduler rebalances them onto the new node
Pods with `PreferNoSchedule` are moved
DaemonSet pods move to the new node
Nothing; scheduling decisions are made once, and only new or recreated pods may land on the new node
explain: The scheduler does not move running pods. New DaemonSet pods are created on the new node, but existing pods stay put unless something (rollout, descheduler, eviction) recreates them.
